answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity earn trust through a verifiable work history: a newcomer locks a small refundable bond and completes independently checked tasks, like water patiently carving a karst valley — slow, observable, and hard to fake at scale. Reputation then grows only as a delta of proven contributions over time, not from how many accounts are created. A fresh identity starts on a low knoll with tiny limits and climbs only through attested work; misbehaviour slashes the bond, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs far more than it can earn.
